answer: Sybil resistance here uses a staked-identity bonding curve: each agent must lock a deposit that grows with its claimed reputation, and peers attest only after an off-chain challenge round. Attackers farming fake identities hit a cost nadir quickly, since every new key requires fresh saffron-priced collateral, while honest agents recover deposits through verified work. A signed echo of each attestation is gossiped to peers, so duplicate keys with identical behavior get flagged and slashed before they can dominate voting.
